exposure: Adherence to national oxytocin administration recommendations
Mode of birth (vaginal birth, assisted vaginal birth, cesarean section)
cohort: 724 women in Robson group 1 (nulliparous women with a single cephalic pregnancy at term, spontaneous onset of labor, and no previous cesarean section)
finding: Oxytocin augmentation was overused in Robson group 1, and early administration, prolonged duration, and slower infusion increases than recommended were associated with cesarean section.
mod_finding: Oxytocin augmentation administered according to national recommendations was associated with a higher likelihood of vaginal birth, while deviations from these recommendations, such as early administration, prolonged duration, and slower infusion increases, were linked to an increased risk of cesarean section.
